request.spec:
A third role, viewer, can be assigned. A viewer sees every screen and figure and can change nothing:
every form submission and every action, including changing the sheet's today, a statement, a hold
and the paste box, is refused with its usual error, writes nothing and changes nothing. A bulk
button (open, settle, reassign, grade, retire, hold, re-date, void) or a generate button (periods, a
fiscal year, quarters, plans) pressed by a viewer goes through with nothing done: its counts show 0
done and every selected item refused, and no error shows; a paste, an import, a rollover and every
other form or action by a viewer is refused with its error.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A third role, viewer, can be assigned. A viewer sees every screen and figure and can change nothing:
every form submission and every action, including changing the sheet's today, a statement, a hold
and the paste box, is refused with its usual error, writes nothing and changes nothing. A bulk
button (open, settle, reassign, grade, retire, hold, re-date, void) or a generate button (periods, a
fiscal year, quarters, plans) pressed by a viewer goes through with nothing done: its counts show 0
done and every selected item refused, and no error shows; a paste, an import, a rollover and every
other form or action by a viewer is refused with its error.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The viewer role is in place, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. Before my change, the two tests that assign a viewer failed and the other two passed.

**Server**
- `viewer` is now a valid role, along with clerk and steward. Any other value, such as `boss`, is still refused. It is stored in the same `role` column, so no migration was needed.
- I added a new first step, `GuardViewer`, to all 23 non-GET endpoint YAMLs. It looks up the signed-in user's role on the sheet. If it is `viewer`, it throws `ViewerRefusedException`, and a new escalation handler turns that into a 403. Because this happens before validation, loading or the rollup, a refused change writes nothing to the store and nothing to the audit file. Read (GET) endpoints are unchanged, so a viewer still sees every screen and figure.
- This covers every form and action: today, settings, rates, roles, people, claims, statements, holds, retire, patrons, periods, quick-add and paste.

**Bulk and generate buttons**
- The bulk Open and Settle buttons send one request per selected claim from the browser. A viewer's requests are each refused, so the button reports 0 done, every claim refused, and no error, which is what the request asks for. I didn't need to change those buttons.
- This app has no other bulk buttons and no generate buttons, so the rest of that part of the request didn't apply.

**Front end**
- The role form's placeholder and error text now mention viewer.
- I fixed one existing bug the test exposed. On a person's row, a refused Statement left its error showing when you then pressed Hold or Retire. That gave two error elements at once and the test timed out. The new `api/rowAction.ts` records the latest action on each row, so only that action's error shows. It is used by the statement, hold, retire and patron cells.

One thing I left alone: the settings that say which roles may open, settle, void, reassign, close or reopen a claim still accept only clerk and steward. Adding viewer there would mean nothing, because a viewer is refused before those settings are checked.
